text: This lesson is a dedicated glossary — a single, organized reference pulling together every core term this course has introduced so far, because Salesforce's vocabulary is dense and mixing up similar-sounding terms is one of the most common ways beginners get tripped up.

From Chapters 2 and 3: an org is your company's own isolated environment. Multitenancy means shared infrastructure with data isolated per org. An instance is the server cluster your org runs on. Edition is your product tier, license is a per-user access grant, metadata is the blueprint behind an org's behavior, and a release is a platform-wide upgrade shipped three times a year.

From Chapter 4: an object is a type of thing tracked, a record is one instance of an object, and a field is one piece of information on a record. An app is a bundle of tabs for one job function, a tab links to one object's records, a list view is a filtered table of those records, and a Home page is an app's landing dashboard.

A few more you'll meet constantly going forward: profiles and permission sets control who can do what, Flow, reports, and dashboards handle automation and visibility, and Sandboxes are where you test safely before an admin deploys changes to Production.

This is the final lesson of this chapter. Next, in the very last lesson of this course, you'll bring everything from all four chapters together and look at how real businesses actually use Salesforce day to day.
